audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly calls Path Maker a block that "intercepts" Tongue Lash (wants.foe[0], whys[2], early, mid, spikes[1]).
audit.why: Riot's text for Path Maker: "K'Sante charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning enemies." That is a damage-reduction charge, not a projectile block, and the derived flags in champ-data/_kits/ksante.json list dash, knockup, hardCC and trueDamage with no blocksProjectiles. Tongue Lash still lands during the charge and still applies its An Acquired Taste stack. The current advice makes a player hold their whole pattern waiting for a block that never happens, and miss the actual threat — the release, which knocks back and stuns.
audit.corrected: Path Maker does not block or intercept anything. It reduces the damage he takes while charging, then releases into a knockback and stun. Your Q still connects and still stacks; what you must not do is dump your commit into the charge window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json — Path Maker description and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: "his Q knockup", "chains his Q stacks into a knockup", dosFull[2] "Dodge his Q knockups", dontsFull[0] "Get walled by his Q" — the entry assigns a knockup to Ntofo Strikes.
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes is a 3.5s, 450-range line that slows, and "At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in." A pull is the opposite direction from a knockup and demands the opposite reaction — you back off from a knockup, you must break range or accept the pull here. The knockback/stun lives on Path Maker (W) and the wall-launch on All Out (R).
audit.corrected: Ntofo Strikes: 3.5s flat, 450 range, slow, and the second stack pulls you in. Knockback and stun are Path Maker. The wall-launch is All Out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json — Ntofo Strikes, Path Maker, All Out

audit.whatIsWrong: content `mid`: "At six your Abyssal Voyage adds global pressure".
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no Abyssal Voyage. His level-6 ability is Devour; the dive is Abyssal Dive (W), available from level 2. The whole "use the global threat to roam and tax" plan built on that sentence is not executable.
audit.corrected: At six you get Devour, which is a duel-ending single-target removal, not map pressure. The level-6 story here is All Out, not a global.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — W Abyssal Dive, R Devour

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0], wants.you[0], whys[1], early and `late` all describe stunning with Tongue Lash and then Devouring.
audit.why: Tongue Lash at 3 stacks "stuns and the stacks are consumed"; Devour needs three stacks to fire on an enemy champion. You cannot do both off one stack set. In `late` this reads "even if he uses R to strip his resists and brawl, you can stun him first and swallow him out of the fight" — a player who tries that in an All Out brawl stuns for a second and then has no ultimate.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys exactly one of the two. Against K'Sante take Devour every time; the stun does not last long enough to matter against a champion with two dashes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — An Acquired Taste, Tongue Lash

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere says that All Out removes Path Maker's stun.
audit.why: Riot's text on Path Maker: "When All Out, deals increased damage and no longer knocks back or stuns." Combined with All Out's own "at the cost of reduced defenses", the brawl after he ultimates is materially safer for a Tahm Kench than the lane exchange before it — he trades his lockdown and his resistances for damage and healing. That inverts the standard "never fight his R form" instinct the entry currently sells in dontsFull[1].
audit.corrected: Once he is All Out he has no stun and reduced resistances. The lethal part of R is the opening wall-launch that separates you from your team, not the duel afterwards.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json — Path Maker ("When All Out ... no longer knocks back or stuns"), All Out

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization never mentions that Path Maker deals true damage, and the content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds at all.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags both resistances-invalidated (Path Maker) and needs-antiheal (All Out) for this pairing. Path Maker's trueDamage flag means armour and MR do nothing against his main lane commit — max HP and grey health do. All Out grants healing, so Grievous Wounds decides the extended fight. Only the full layer's breakdown.late mentions anti-heal, in passing.
audit.corrected: Buy HP over resistances against Path Maker's true damage — Heartsteel is the correct first item for this matchup, not just a generic pick. Grievous Wounds is mandatory before you contest an All Out fight.
sources: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json (resistances-invalidated, needs-antiheal); champ-data/_kits/ksante.json — Path Maker trueDamage, All Out heal

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[1].why (Level 2) says "Only take the trade when K'Sante's All Out is down", and the whole cooldown block tracks All Out.
audit.why: K'Sante has no ultimate at level 2. The lane-defining cooldown is Path Maker at 14/13/12/11/10s; All Out is 120/100/80s and only matters from 6. Telling a player to gate every level-2 trade on a spell that does not exist yet means they either never trade or ignore the advice.
audit.corrected: Lane cooldown is Path Maker, 14s at rank 1. Ntofo Strikes is 3.5s so it is effectively always up. All Out is 120s at rank 1 and only enters the picture at 6.

audit.why: 49.05% over 789 games against a chart of Tahm Kench 3 / K'Sante 3 / Skill 1 is consistent, and EVEN 6/10 fits. No edit.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online — land Tongue Lash to slow him, auto twice, then stun and Devour before his W block is ready to punish your all-in.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online — Tongue Lash to slow, auto twice, then spend the stacks on Devour, not on the stun that eats them, with Path Maker down.

edits.before: K'Sante's Q knockup and W dash-block let him dictate short trades freely — don't overextend without the stun ready, or he chains his Q stacks into a knockup and wins the exchange.
edits.after: Ntofo Strikes is 3.5s and its second stack pulls you in, not up; Path Maker is the knockback and stun, on 14s. Trade once Path Maker is spent — nothing else there locks you down.

edits.after: Stack An Acquired Taste to three with Tongue Lash poke and autos, then spend all three on Devour — the Q stun consumes the very same stacks

edits.after: Chain Ntofo Strikes to two stacks so the shockwave pulls you in, then release Path Maker to stun you

edits.before: At level one Tongue Lash's range and slow let you contest the wave and start stacking An Acquired Taste without giving him a free Q-stack opportunity — he can chip you with Q but your Thick Skin converts it passively and he has no kill threat yet. At level two you want to reach three stacks as fast as possible: land Tongue Lash, walk up for two autos, and the moment the stun is ready you can Devour him for a punishing trade he has zero answer to if his W block is on cooldown. Level three is where you have to be honest — his Q knockup chain is also fully online and his W can block your Tongue Lash, so fish for stacks only when you see his W spent on something, never commit the Devour into an available W dash.
edits.after: At level one Tongue Lash's 900 range and slow let you contest the wave and start stacking An Acquired Taste from outside Ntofo Strikes' 450 — he can chip you but Thick Skin converts it passively and he has no kill threat yet. At level two reach three stacks as fast as possible: land Tongue Lash, walk up for two autos, then Devour — do not fire the stun first, because it consumes the exact stacks Devour needs. Level three is where you have to be honest: Path Maker (14s) does not block Tongue Lash, it eats damage while charging and then knocks you back and stuns, so commit only once he has spent it. Ntofo Strikes is a flat 3.5s — treat it as permanently up, never as your window.

edits.before: Levels four and five are the lane's most dangerous window for you: K'Sante can block your stun with W, chain his own Q stacks into a knockup, and win burst exchanges you cannot heal through fast enough without your item spike. Play for CS, use Tongue Lash at max range to fish stacks at a safe angle, and activate Thick Skin proactively to shield rather than waiting for him to chunk you. At six your Abyssal Voyage adds global pressure but does not fundamentally flip the 1v1 — your best play is to use the global threat to roam and tax, coming back to lane with the item spike that finally tilts sustained trades back your way.
edits.after: Levels four and five are the lane's most dangerous window for you: K'Sante eats your commit inside Path Maker's charge, pulls you in on the second Ntofo Strikes stack, and wins burst exchanges you cannot heal through without your item spike. Play for CS, use Tongue Lash at max range to fish stacks at a safe angle, and activate Thick Skin proactively to shield rather than waiting for him to chunk you. At six All Out throws you through a wall away from your tower — but it strips his own resistances and removes Path Maker's stun, so the brawl after suits you if you already hold Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: First item Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis is your real power spike: Thick Skin grey health scales with your max HP, so the longer he spends trading Q autos into you the more your shield becomes when you pop E, and Devour's bonus damage at three stacks starts to genuinely hurt him. At two-plus items you are near-unkillable in extended fights and your point-and-click Devour removes him entirely whenever he tries to engage — even if he uses R to strip his resists and brawl, you can stun him first and swallow him out of the fight. Never let him isolate you one-versus-one when his R is up; keep your team close and use Devour as the engagement reset that wins teamfights rather than a solo-kill tool.
edits.after: First item Heartsteel is your real power spike, and it is the right item specifically here: Path Maker deals true damage, so armour and MR do nothing against his main commit while max HP feeds Thick Skin's grey-health shield. At two-plus items your point-and-click Devour removes him whenever he engages, but All Out heals him through chip, so Grievous Wounds is not optional. Never let him isolate you when R is up — it launches you back through any wall in the way, and that displacement away from your team is what actually kills you, not the duel that follows it. Once he is All Out, Path Maker no longer stuns at all, so if the wall-launch misses, the brawl afterwards is yours to take.

edits.before: Three stacks of An Acquired Taste are online and his W is on a longer cooldown than your Devour window — stun him and swallow him for a trade he cannot block or escape.
edits.after: Three stacks arm Devour, and the Tongue Lash stun consumes those same stacks — swallow him rather than stunning, ideally with Path Maker's 14s already spent.

edits.before: His W dash-block fully intercepts Tongue Lash if he anticipates it, and his own Q stacks lead to a knockup combo that beats you in a straight exchange — only engage when W is visibly on cooldown.
edits.after: Path Maker does not block Tongue Lash — it charges through the damage, then knocks you back and stuns; the second Ntofo Strikes stack pulls you in. Engage only once Path Maker is spent.

edits.before: His R lets him strip resistances and brawl as a fighter rather than a tank, and you have no reliable way to Devour him out of an R-activated isolation — respect the all-in and stay near teammates.
edits.after: All Out launches you back through any wall and away from your team; it also strips his own resistances and removes Path Maker's stun, so the danger is the displacement, not the duel.

edits.before: Q-stun at 3 stacks is your kill switch. Only take the trade when K'Sante's All Out is down.
edits.after: 3 stacks arm Devour, not the Q stun. Trade when K'Sante's Path Maker (14s) is down.

edits.before: - K'Sante All Out: matchup-defining — His duelist mode. Trade when down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - K'Sante Path Maker: 14s rank 1 — the lane cooldown; the charge is damage reduction, not a block. - Ntofo Strikes: 3.5s, pulls on the 2nd stack. - All Out: 120s, strips his own resists.

edits.before: Lick K'Sante to 3 stacks in short exchanges, Q-stun when his answer is down, and Devour the all-in under your wave.
edits.after: Lick K'Sante to 3 stacks in short exchanges, then spend them on Devour once Path Maker is down — not on the Q stun.

notes: The packet defect "never names any of K'Sante's abilities" was accurate for the content layer — every reference was "his Q / his W / his R". Both wrong mechanics followed from that vagueness: a Q knockup that is really a pull, and a W block that is really damage reduction. The full layer already named All Out but gated level-2 trades on it, which is impossible. I did not touch full report[] entries that duplicate tradeGood and breakdown.trading verbatim; if report is not regenerated from those fields it still carries the stun-into-Devour line.
